links.outcome: Readability age of LLM patient education responses
links.effect: Average readability age of 13.3 ± 1.2 years, difficulty score 13.2 ± 1.2, sentence length 51.5 ± 12.5 words across three models without simplification prompt.
links.quote: For readability and complexity, the three models achieved an average readability age of 13.3 ± 1.2 years, a difficulty score of 13.2 ± 1.2, a total word count of 285.6 ± 128.5, and a sentence length of 51.5 ± 12.5 words.

links.outcome: Reading level of LLM patient education answers (readability age)
links.effect: Mean readability age 13.3 ± 1.2 years without prompt; simplification prompt lowered DouBao's from 12.9 ± 0.8 to 10.1 ± 1.2 years (p<0.01) and GPT-4's from 13.4 to 12.2 years.
links.quote: DouBao had significant reductions in readability age (12.9 ± 0.8 vs. 10.1 ± 1.2 years, p < 0.01), difficulty score (12.7 ± 0.7 vs. 10.6 ± 1.1, p < 0.01), total word count (283.0 ± 90.6 vs. 138.7 ± 28.7, p < 0.01), and sentence length (50.7 ± 15.6 vs. 36.0 ± 9.6 words, p < 0.01).

links.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy of LLM cardio-oncology patient education responses
links.effect: 63.3% correct, 35.0% partially correct, 1.7% incorrect across 240 responses; no significant accuracy difference between models (p=0.26).
links.quote: The distribution of accuracy ratings for the combined question set across all three models is as follows: 63.3% ( n = 152, 95% CI: 57.2–69.4%) of responses were rated as “correct,” 35.0% ( n = 84, 95% CI: 29.0–41.0%) as “partially correct,” and 1.7% ( n = 4, 95% CI: 0–3.3%) as “incorrect” ( Figure 1 ).

links.outcome: Response quality change when prompt asks for simple language versus no prompt
links.effect: Simplification prompt lowered accuracy (Kimi 70.0% vs 48.8%, p<0.01; DouBao 57.5% vs 7.5%, p<0.01; GPT-4 62.5% vs 51.2%, p=0.15) and comprehensiveness, helpfulness, practicality (p<0.01 all).
links.quote: In accuracy, GPT-4 exhibited the smallest decline (62.5% vs. 51.2%, p = 0.15), while Kimi (70.0% vs. 48.8%, p < 0.01) and DouBao (57.5% vs. 7.5%, p < 0.01) showed significant reductions.

links.quote: Statistically significant differences were observed among the three models in comprehensiveness ( p = 0.03) and helpfulness ( p < 0.01) ( Figure 2 ), while no significant difference was found in practicality ( p = 0.28) ( Figure 2 ).

links.effect: DouBao readability age decreased from 12.9 ± 0.8 to 10.1 ± 1.2 years (p<0.01), but accuracy decreased 57.5% to 7.5% (p<0.01).
links.quote: While simplifying language improves readability, it risks compromising clinical relevance.
